newsitem.title: USA: Dow Industrials seen higher after another record.
newsitem.headline: Dow Industrials seen higher after another record.

text.p: The Dow Industrials are seen moving higher with bonds at the opening on Thursday following their tenth record close this month and their first one above the 6400 mark.
Analysts said that high tech stocks remained among the market leaders and that they would be joined today by the autos which were higher in London overnight.
"The futures are firmer so we'll start on the upside and then see if we can sustain it," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities.
The Dow rally was accompanied by a broad market in which gainers led losers by narrow margins. Wachtel said the lack of confirmation was a sign that the broad market was correcting.
"There is a correction happening while the Dow rocks on. There is no telling where the industrials will stop," he said.
He said that high techs would continue to surge despite profit-taking which set later in the day on Wednesday.

"IBM got tired when it reached 159. A lot of analysts had put their price target at 160," Wachtel said. "But high techs are still the cutting edge and they will continue to flourish, hitting a wall from time to time."
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average was down 47 points at 21,143.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index was down two at 3961.

Among U.S. shares traded in London, General Motors Corp was up 3/8 at 57-1/2, Chrysler Corp was up 1/4 at 34-1/2 and Ford Motor Co was up 1/8 at 32-5/8. International Business Machines Corp was up 1/2 at 153-1/4, Texas Instruments Inc rose 1/4 to 55-1/4 and Digital Equipment Corp rose 1/4 to 35-1/4.
The dollar was firm against the yen and in a narrow range in Europe.
The long bond was up 6/32 to yield 6.40 percent.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street writes that International Business Machines is riding a wave of panic buying of blue chip stocks like Coca-Cola Co and Intel Corp.
The New York Times writes that while the stock prices of computer makers are rising, those of computer retailers like CompUSA, Circuit City Stores Inc and Best Buy Co Inc are not.
